claims.text: On Bag, foo="2" is coerced to integer 2; annotated extra-key length and value schemas reject long and noninteger values independently.
The __pydantic_extra__ annotation configures extra storage/schema, not an ordinary field: Bag.model_fields contains count only.

strict=True rejects the numeric string extra as int_type; extra=ignore discards long/bad without extra validation; extra=forbid rejects foo as extra_forbidden. model_validate forwards these options to the core validator.

IgnoredBag was compiled with ignore, so the allow-only schema-generation condition did not supply its annotated extra key/value validators; overriding to allow stores long="bad" without enforcing those constraints.

The override-created object exposes long="bad" via __pydantic_extra__ and attribute lookup, while its ordinary model_dump is {count:1}; runtime validation extra policy does not rebuild the class serializer. The omitted extra is an observed pinned-core result, not evidence that storage failed.

critical_errors: Claiming runtime extra=allow regenerates the annotated extra schema for an ignore-configured model.
Claiming missing extra data in model_dump proves it was not stored.
Claiming Field(init=False) disables validation of extra values.

claims.text: For Derived and Checked the required one-argument factory receives previously validated a as integer 3, not the raw string.
Derived.b is string "6" because defaults are not validated by default; Checked.b is integer 6 because validate_default=True applies the integer schema.
The detector requires exactly one positional-capable parameter with no default. optional(data=None) is treated as a zero-argument factory and produces 99.
Invalid a produces int_parsing at a plus default_factory_not_called at b; derive is not invoked after that validation failure.
Providing b="8" validates it to integer 8 and does not invoke the default factory.
Reordered invokes derive before a has been validated, so data has no a and a KeyError propagates; supplying a in the input does not make it available early.

critical_errors: Claiming annotation b:int always validates the factory result.
Claiming an optional data parameter receives validated data.

claims.text: The first present alias legacy supplies value; default forbid reports payload and value as extra inputs. With extra=ignore the same input yields value=1.
Payload-only yields value=2, name-only yields value=3, and a missing index in an empty payload path allows the enabled name fallback yielding 3 when extras are ignored.
A present legacy="bad" produces int_parsing at legacy; it does not retry the later valid payload alias.
Explicit by_alias=False, by_name=True with extra=ignore selects value="3" and yields integer 3 from the all-keys input.
by_alias=True dumping uses out; normal dumping uses value. out is not a validation alias, so out-only input yields missing legacy and extra_forbidden at out.
Passing by_alias=False while omitting runtime by_name raises PydanticUserError before core validation, despite the class having validate_by_name=True: the Python guard tests the explicit arguments.
